source_claims.claim: Before Theorem 14.8, the source introduces triangular-array rows X_{n,1},...,X_{n,k_n}, row-wise independence on a common probability space, possibly different probability spaces for different rows, zero means, variances sigma_{n,i}^2, s_n^2 as the row variance sum, and s_n^2 -> infinity.

For every epsilon > 0, s_n^{-2} times the row sum of E[X_{n,i}^2 1{|X_{n,i}| >= epsilon s_n}] tends to 0; the source identifies this expectation with the integral of x^2 over |x| >= epsilon s_n against the law induced by X_{n,i}.
There exists delta > 0 such that s_n^{-(2+delta)} times the row sum of E[|X_{n,i}|^{2+delta}] tends to 0.
The source states that the Lyapunov condition is stronger than the Lindeberg condition.
Under either Lindeberg or Lyapunov, the standardized row sums converge in distribution to N(0,1).
The source explicitly says the proof is beyond the scope of the book and refers readers to external sources.
